I find that the lack of upvotes you can give out until you get a certain amount yourself is kind of stifling the community. If you need 20 points to get more votes, but everyone only has 10 a day, that requires 2 people to spend their entire days worth just for you to have more. It just seems like it'll hurt anyone who tries to join in.

Lack of HTTPS. I think it should be on by default. Online services where people discuss potentially personal things should leak as little information as possible. (Reddit has refused to roll out site wide HTTPS for years.)

If I were to compare it to Reddit and assuming comparable features since this is a fork of Reddit's code...

Reddit's moderation tools are lackluster. Getting WV's up to snuff and perhaps even better than Reddit's would be a big plus.

Examples:

  • Only one sticky per subreddit - this is useful, but the limit of one is, well, limiting.
  • You can't make moderation logs public. Some subreddits would like to do that but there is no truly transparent verifiable option.
  • Automoderator fills a lot of holes such as automatic messaging based on content. (As an example, someone posts "Hey, you posted a link that's banned in this subreddit so your link was removed.) This kind of feature should be built in and not relying on a bot if possible.

That's just off the top of my head.

So not things wrong insomuch as improvements you can make over the originator if you take the time.
